chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that a slave girl was bought for him from Kufa. He said:

So she went to attend to one of the needs, and she said, 'O mother!' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to her: 'Do you have a mother?' She said, 'Yes'. So he ordered that she be returned, and said: 'I do not feel safe if I were to keep her, from seeing in my children what I dislike.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) return a slave girl he had purchased?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Imam’s (peace be upon him) sensitivity to familial bonds even within the institution of slavery, illustrating the principle that ownership does not negate kinship ties. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that separating a mother from her child is a source of emotional distress ('what one dislikes') and thus merited compensation or return, reflecting the broader ethical imperative of preserving family integrity in Islamic jurisprudence.
